## docs/api.md

21 findings — 0 blocker, 17 major, 4 minor, 0 nit.

### [major] `methods : [HttpMethod]` uses list syntax no production admits and no type system defines

- **Where:** docs/api.md:43, docs/schema/railroad.md:93, docs/schema/railroad.md:94, docs/schema/types.md:6
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/railroad.md (Types) and docs/schema/types.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:43 — `  methods     : [HttpMethod],     -- which HTTP methods to expose (default: all)`. railroad.md:93-96 — `TypeExpr ::= Variant ( '|' Variant )*` / `Variant ::= QName TypeArg* | '(' TypeExpr ( ',' TypeExpr )+ ')'` / `TypeArg ::= QName | Literal`. A grep for `[` in railroad.md's EBNF blocks returns only character classes (lines 26, 34, 35, 38, 751) — `[` and `]` are not tokens anywhere. types.md lists no list, array, or set type.
- **Why it is wrong:** The declaration does not parse, and there is no collection type by design: multi-valued structure is a `Component` sub-table. This is the first schema declaration a reader of api.md meets, so it teaches Haskell list syntax that the language does not have.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Auto-Generated Routes", replace `methods : [HttpMethod],` with a `Component` sub-table on the route row — `methods :> RouteMethod : Component { method : HttpMethod, unique m { method } }` — or five `Bool` columns, and say which. Add a one-line bullet to railroad.md's Types constraint list: "There is no collection type; multi-valued structure is a `Component` sub-table (see tables.md)."

### [major] Route tables carry `Configuration`, whose rows deliberately do not live on the branch, yet routes are claimed to resolve per schema node

- **Where:** docs/api.md:41, docs/api.md:69, docs/api.md:120, docs/distribution.md:245
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md (Auto-Generated Routes / Custom Routes), consistent with docs/distribution.md#schema-shards-are-rooted-at-a-branch
- **Evidence:** api.md:41 `table system.api.GeneratedRoute : Configuration {`; api.md:69 `table system.api.CustomRoute : Configuration {`; api.md:120-123 "Custom routes are schema objects — they are committed to the transaction graph and are naturally included or excluded based on which schema node a version token resolves to." Against distribution.md:243-246, whose table puts "Schema nodes: types, tables, traits, functors, **routes**" and "`Reference` rows, because inserting one *is* a schema transaction" on the branch shard, and "`Configuration` rows — operator tuning that must survive a merge" explicitly elsewhere.
- **Why it is wrong:** distribution.md names routes as branch-shard schema nodes in the same table that excludes `Configuration` rows from the branch. As declared, a route added on `experiment-checkout` is visible on `main` immediately and a version token cannot exclude it — the opposite of api.md:120-123. The trait choice is load-bearing twice over: functions.md:220 uses `Configuration` to forbid function literals in exactly this table.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md, retrait both declarations to `: Reference` (a route registration is code selection; inserting a `Reference` row is already a schema transaction — traits.md#reference-tables-are-code). Move genuinely operational fields (`enabled`) to a separate `Configuration` override table, and restate api.md:94 as "takes effect when the branch ref advances" rather than "immediately".

### [major] api.md teaches monotonic integer schema versions and omits every OQ-026 HTTP-surface rule

- **Where:** docs/api.md:14, docs/api.md:18, docs/api.md:19, docs/api.md:25, docs/api.md:33, docs/transaction-graph.md:34, docs/transaction-graph.md:94
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md (Versioning and Backwards Compatibility); resolution model stays in docs/transaction-graph.md#branches-tags-and-version-tokens
- **Evidence:** api.md:18-19 `/v{N}/records/…` and `/v{N}/api/…`; api.md:25 "A client pinned to `/v3/...` continues working after the schema advances to version 10." Against api.md:33 nineteen lines later ("Version tokens may be a graph node hash prefix, a tag, or a branch name"), transaction-graph.md:34 which writes the path as `/v{token}/records/...`, and OQ-026 (open-questions.md:125-138) which lists no integer counter. transaction-graph.md:94-104 owns no-version routing to `main` HEAD, A/B splitting with session affinity, the `/vcurrent/` alias, and the `/versions` discovery endpoint — none of which appear in api.md.
- **Why it is wrong:** There is no monotone integer version anywhere in the design; the graph is a DAG with branches, so "advances to version 10" is not well defined across two branches. The document contradicts itself within one section, and the five behaviours an implementer needs to build the router live in the document about the transaction graph rather than the one titled "Custom APIs and HTTP Dispatch".
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Versioning and Backwards Compatibility": replace `{N}` with `{token}` in every path, and rewrite line 25 as "A client pinned to `/vv2.1.0/...` or to a hash prefix continues to resolve after `main` advances." Add a subsection carrying the HTTP-surface half of OQ-026 — unversioned requests route to `main` HEAD, optional A/B split with session affinity, the `/vcurrent/` alias, the `/versions` endpoint — and leave transaction-graph.md owning token *resolution*, linked one way. While there, reconcile api.md:6 ("no route is ever removed") with api.md:102 ("Removing the custom route restores auto-generated behavior").

### [major] `system.logs.HttpRequest` declares `server_id : ServerId` and `received_at`, re-creating stored columns the virtual columns already project

- **Where:** docs/api.md:191, docs/api.md:192, docs/schema/tables.md:26, docs/schema/tables.md:30, docs/open-questions.md:399
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/tables.md (virtual columns) / docs/transaction-graph.md#virtual-columns
- **Evidence:** api.md:191-192 `  server_id     : ServerId,` / `  received_at   : Timestamp,`. tables.md:24-30 — every table has `created_at` and `origin_server` ("the issuing server, extracted from the row's `DataId`, typed `:> system.shards.Node`"), and "The first two are projections of the row's identifier and cost no bytes and no lookup." OQ-005 (open-questions.md:399) — "`system.shards.LogSegment` had been hand-rolling this projection as a declared `server` field; that field is **removed** … **`origin_server`** is typed `:> system.shards.Node` rather than `Int` — as a bare 2-byte integer every 'which server wrote this' query is a manual join against a magic number."
- **Why it is wrong:** This reintroduces on the highest-volume table in the system the exact defect OQ-005 removed from `LogSegment`: a stored column duplicating a `DataId` projection, typed as a bare identifier (`ServerId`, defined nowhere) rather than `:> system.shards.Node`. `received_at` likewise duplicates `created_at` unless it is deliberately the pre-dispatch timestamp, which the document does not say.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "HTTP Request Logging", delete `server_id : ServerId` and add one sentence: "The writing server is the `origin_server` virtual column (see [schema/tables.md](schema/tables.md#basic-syntax))." Delete `received_at` in favour of `created_at`, or keep it and state explicitly that it is the pre-dispatch arrival time and differs from row-write time by `duration`.

### [major] `system.logs.HttpRequest` field names in api.md disagree with the `RequestRollup` binding in aggregates.md

- **Where:** docs/api.md:190, docs/api.md:196, docs/api.md:197, docs/schema/aggregates.md:12, docs/schema/aggregates.md:191, docs/schema/aggregates.md:213
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md (the `system.logs.HttpRequest` declaration); docs/schema/aggregates.md should cite it
- **Evidence:** api.md:190-202 declares `status_code : Int`, `duration_ms : Int`, and no bytes column. aggregates.md:12-18 — `RequestRollup g = system.logs.HttpRequest group { truncateTo g created_at as bucket_start, status } { bucket_start, status, count rows as requests, sum rows.bytes_sent as bytes, max rows.duration as slowest }`. aggregates.md:191-193 — `retain system.logs.HttpRequest as RequestRollup where status >= 500`. aggregates.md:213 — "In the example, `status` is a group key, so every bucket row is wholly 5xx or wholly not."
- **Why it is wrong:** The only end-to-end `retain` chain in the docs reads three columns from a table whose declaration has none of them; two are near-misses of declared names. `duration_ms : Int` also contradicts types.md:188-196 ("unit names are **constants**") — the unit belongs in the type, not the field name.
- **Fix:** Pick one name set in docs/api.md (the declaration home): add `bytes_sent : Int`, rename `status_code` → `status`, and rename `duration_ms : Int` → `duration : Duration`. Then have aggregates.md cite the declaration rather than assume field names.

### [major] api.md says view refresh resolves inside the transaction; storage.md runs it on the maintenance queue

- **Where:** docs/api.md:147, docs/storage.md:69, docs/storage.md:200, docs/schema/functors.md:19, docs/open-questions.md:146
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/storage.md (Materialization)
- **Evidence:** api.md:147 — "Internal event functors (index updates, view refresh) resolve within the transaction as they occur." storage.md:69-71 — "It runs under the event scheduler on `system.events.MaintenanceQueue` alongside compaction and view refresh, pegged to a stable commit node the way a materialized view computation is." storage.md:200-205 — "A materialized view is pegged to a **specific commit node** … It never blocks or slows ongoing transactions, because it references a past, stable state. It is updated in the background, or lazily on access." functors.md:19-21 — "Kind 4 is asynchronous and decoupled: the commit always succeeds (inserting the queue row is the commit)."
- **Why it is wrong:** View refresh is a background maintenance-queue job pegged to a past commit node, precisely so it never blocks a transaction. api.md inverts that and would make every write pay refresh cost. "Internal event functors" is also not a category the four-kind model has — kind 4 always enqueues.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Transaction Semantics", split line 147: "Index updates are part of the commit. View refresh and repartitioning are queued on `system.events.MaintenanceQueue` and run outside it — see [storage.md](storage.md#materialization)." Drop the phrase "internal event functors". Apply the same correction to the "Event functors" bullet of OQ-027 (open-questions.md:146), which carries the same wording.

### [major] Custom-route path shape is internally inconsistent: `/api/` prefix, leading slash, and `/records/` shadowing cannot all hold

- **Where:** docs/api.md:19, docs/api.md:70, docs/api.md:99, docs/api.md:105, docs/api.md:113
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md (Custom Routes / Route Conflict Resolution)
- **Evidence:** api.md:19 — `/v{N}/api/orders/{id}/ship             -- custom endpoint at version N`. api.md:70 — `  route_template : Text unique,     -- e.g. "/orders/{id}/ship"`. api.md:99-101 — "If a custom route is registered at `/records/app.commerce.Order/{id}`, it handles all requests to that path". api.md:105 — "Custom routes whose template starts with `raw/` are rejected at insert time." api.md:113 — "A custom route registered under the `/records/` prefix must reference a table or view that exists."
- **Why it is wrong:** Three incompatible readings. If `/api/` is prepended to `route_template`, a template of `/records/app.commerce.Order/{id}` lands at `/v{N}/api/records/…` and can never shadow the generated route, contradicting :99-101 and :113. The reserved-prefix check is written without a leading slash (`raw/`) while the shadowing and validation rules use one (`/records/`), so `"/raw/app.commerce.Order/{id}"` passes the check the check exists to enforce. The document never says whether the template is stored with a leading slash or whether the version segment is part of it, so the trie cannot be built from this.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Route Conflict Resolution", state one normalization rule: `route_template` is an absolute path below the version segment — leading slash required, version segment excluded, no trailing slash — mounted directly at `/v{token}<template>`. Restate the reserved check against the normalized form: "a normalized template whose first segment is `raw` is rejected at insert time". Delete the `/api/` segment from line 19 or fold it into the template at line 70. Apply the same leading-slash correction to OQ-028 (open-questions.md:178).

### [major] `system.logs.HttpRequest` called "subject to time-bounded retention" though silence means keep and no chain is declared

- **Where:** docs/api.md:221, docs/api.md:190, docs/schema/aggregates.md:286, docs/schema/traits.md:107, docs/schema/railroad.md:417, docs/open-questions.md:536
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/aggregates.md (Pruning is only ever a consequence); the declaration belongs in docs/api.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:221 — "- **Prunable** — subject to the same time-bounded retention as other `LogData` shards", on a table declared at :190 with no `retain` statement anywhere in api.md. Against aggregates.md:286-296 — "**`LogData` is prunable, not pruned. A row is discarded only when a `retain` chain says its retention has expired.** … a `LogData` table with no `retain` statement is **never pruned at all**. … Silence means keep."; traits.md:107-111 the same; railroad.md:417-419 — "`prune` naming a `LogData` table is rejected."
- **Why it is wrong:** OQ-032 identifies this exact wording as the defect it fixed. As written, api.md tells an operator that HTTP request rows age out automatically; under the settled rule they are kept forever, because no chain is declared. Given api.md:187 ("the only write that DataCode guarantees on every request path") and api.md:206 ("the highest-risk sink in the system for a value that should never have been persisted"), unbounded retention is the consequential reading and the opposite of what the bullet says. The two `retain system.logs.HttpRequest` occurrences in aggregates.md are worked examples of chain syntax, not declarations of this table's policy.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "HTTP Request Logging", replace the bullet with "**Retained by policy** — kept indefinitely unless a `retain` chain is declared for it; see [schema/aggregates.md](schema/aggregates.md#retain)." If DataCode ships a default chain, declare it in api.md next to the table (e.g. `retain system.logs.HttpRequest as RequestRollup for 1 day , by Hour for 1 month , by Day for 6 month , by Month forever`) and have aggregates.md's examples cite it rather than invent one.

### [major] api.md's authentication rule requires a *client* token specifically and forbids the login and webhook-ingress routes from existing

- **Where:** docs/api.md:152, docs/auth.md:14, docs/auth.md:19, docs/auth.md:36, docs/events.md:34, docs/events.md:45, docs/open-questions.md:402
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md#authentication-and-authorization, with token types owned by docs/auth.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:152-154 — "Every request to any route — auto-generated or custom — must carry a valid client token and user token. There is no mechanism to create an unauthenticated DataCode endpoint." Against auth.md:14 — "Every request requires **two tokens**: one from the first group and one user token", where the first group is Server Token *or* Client Token (auth.md:16-27); auth.md:36-41 — "Initial login: User presents a credential … Server issues per-device session token"; and OQ-005 (open-questions.md:402) — "**Inbound arrival is not an event.** A webhook … is a route whose functor inserts into a landing table." events.md:34 names api.md as the home for inbound routes and events.md:45 hands the security question to it; a grep of api.md finds no occurrence of "webhook", "signature", or "landing table".
- **Why it is wrong:** Three defects. Server-to-server and localhost traffic carries a server token, not a client token, so the rule excludes the two callers that exercise the API most. The login exchange cannot present the user token it exists to obtain, so the route performing it is a counterexample to the stated invariant. And an external provider signing with HMAC holds no DataCode token at all, so the settled webhook pattern is unrepresentable — OQ-020 tracks *how* to authenticate one, but nothing tracks that the blanket rule forbids the endpoint.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Authentication and Authorization", replace lines 152-154 with: "Every request carries a server or client token (see [auth.md](auth.md#token-types)); every request that reads or writes application data also carries a user token." Name the exempt set explicitly — the credential-exchange route and signature-authenticated ingress routes. Add an "Inbound routes" subsection covering the landing-table pattern and stating that an ingress route authenticates as a named service account (OQ-015), so the write stays attributable; cite OQ-020 as the open part.

### [major] api.md describes authorization as asserts only, omitting client-token scope and default-deny namespace grants

- **Where:** docs/api.md:156, docs/auth.md:417, docs/namespaces.md:119, docs/schema/constraints.md:253
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/auth.md and docs/namespaces.md#namespace-access-control
- **Evidence:** api.md:156-160 — "**Authorization** is automatic and derived from the access control functors on the tables the API functor accesses. No per-route permission declaration exists." Against auth.md:417-418 — "Composition: a request's access is the intersection of the client token's schema-level access and the user token's row-level access"; namespaces.md:119 — "The model is **default-deny with recursive grants** (OQ-024)"; constraints.md:250-264, which places client scope and `bypass access` above row-level asserts.
- **Why it is wrong:** Authorization has three layers and api.md names one. Omitting default-deny grants inverts the default an implementer would build: as written, a route reaching a table with no access asserts is open to every authenticated user, where namespaces.md says it is denied absent a grant. Omitting client scope drops the schema-level half of the intersection, and `bypass access` / `bypass erasure` go unmentioned on the page that describes request handling.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md, restate the Authorization paragraph as three conditions: a request is authorized iff (1) the client token's namespace scope covers every table touched, (2) the user token holds a recursive grant reaching each, and (3) every `assert` mentioning `authed_user` passes — unless the grant carries `bypass access`. Link [auth.md](auth.md#token-types) and [namespaces.md](namespaces.md#namespace-access-control) as the homes rather than restating their rules.

### [major] No HTTP status-code mapping, and "all known failure modes return 4xx" is wrong for the file's own unavailability case

- **Where:** docs/api.md:138, docs/api.md:141, docs/api.md:79, docs/open-questions.md:147
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md#transaction-semantics
- **Evidence:** api.md:136-139 — "The transaction is atomic — it either fully commits or fully fails … 500s should be avoided; all known failure modes return 4xx." Immediately followed by :141-145 — "a **cluster-wide mutation is not one transaction** … applied by each shard primary independently and may be partial; its result is a per-shard report naming which shards contributed, not an all-or-nothing status code." OQ-027 (open-questions.md:147) cites "shard 47 is down" as a state the return value must express.
- **Why it is wrong:** A shard being unreachable is server-side; returning 4xx blames the client and breaks retry semantics for every conforming HTTP client and proxy. Beyond that, the document gives no mapping for the failure modes it defines elsewhere: validation failure, access denial (403 versus 200-with-`Redacted`), FK violation, a prepared-node abort from a concurrent conflict, `enforce forward` coercion, a `Sealed` value requiring `reveal`, and a partially applied cluster-wide mutation. api.md:79 mentions 405 in isolation. An implementer cannot build the error path.
- **Fix:** Add a status-code table to docs/api.md "Transaction Semantics" with one row per named failure mode. Replace the blanket rule with: "Client-attributable failures are 4xx; unavailability is 503 with `Retry-After`; a partial cluster-wide mutation is 202 plus a subscription handle." State the error-body shape and that it must not carry the offending value (api.md:205-211).

### [major] An "API functor" names no declared function type, so it carries no signature and no effect index

- **Where:** docs/api.md:71, docs/api.md:86, docs/api.md:90, docs/api.md:44, docs/api.md:55, docs/schema/functions.md:173, docs/schema/functions.md:186
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md (route tables), with the function-type rule in docs/schema/functions.md#function-types
- **Evidence:** api.md:71 `get_functor    : FunctorRef | NotAllowed,`; api.md:86-88 "Each referenced functor is an **API functor**: it receives the extracted path parameters and request body (if present), performs reads and/or writes within a single transaction, and returns a response value"; api.md:90 "There is no separate API functor type — field types are referenced directly from the schema everywhere they are used." Against functions.md:173-179 — "**A field may not write an arrow inline; it names a declared function type.** … **Every function in a field shares one signature**, by construction, because a field has a type" — and functions.md:186-189, which cites `system.api.CustomRoute` as the exemplar of a function-typed column whose "compiler knows the signature". No `RouteHandler` or equivalent type is declared anywhere.
- **Why it is wrong:** `FunctorRef` is the storage representation, not a declared function type, so the column carries no signature and the guarantee functions.md states fails on the table it names as the example. The effect is likewise unindexed: api.md:86 has the handler writing (`Tx`) while api.md:55's format functor merely "transforms query results" (`Read`), yet both are the same `FunctorRef`, so the effect ladder cannot enforce "no external calls inside a commit" on a custom route. The typing of path captures — differing in arity across `/orders/{id}/ship` and `/reports/{y}/{m}/{table}` — is consequently unspecified too.
- **Fix:** Declare the signatures in docs/api.md and type the columns against them: `type RouteHandler = RouteRequest -> Tx RouteResponse` where `RouteRequest` carries `path_params : Doc`, `body : Doc`, and the sample moment, and `type FormatFunctor = Table -> Read Bytes`. Change `get_functor : FunctorRef | NotAllowed` to `get_handler : RouteHandler | NotAllowed` (same for post/put/patch/delete) and `functor_ref : FunctorRef` to `functor : FormatFunctor`. State the commit-time check binding a template's captures to `path_params`.

### [major] `route_template : Text unique` does not detect the conflicts api.md credits it with

- **Where:** docs/api.md:70, docs/api.md:82, docs/api.md:117, docs/open-questions.md:191
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md#custom-routes
- **Evidence:** api.md:70 `route_template : Text unique,     -- e.g. "/orders/{id}/ship"`; api.md:82-84 "`route_template` is the table's candidate key, which is also what makes exact-path conflicts a schema validation error at insert time rather than a bespoke check — the trie's handler slot can only hold one handler, and the key says so (see OQ-028 and OQ-029)." Against OQ-029 (open-questions.md:191) — "exact-path conflicts are a schema validation error at insert time. The trie's `nodeHandler` slot can only hold one handler; inserting a duplicate pattern is rejected."
- **Why it is wrong:** `/orders/{id}/ship` and `/orders/{order_id}/ship` are distinct `Text` values that compile to the same trie pattern, so the `unique` on the raw string does not catch the conflict. OQ-029 attributes the check to the trie's `nodeHandler` slot, which is a bespoke check, not to the key — api.md:82 claims the opposite. Secondarily, a table-wide `unique` on the raw template makes it unclear how two live versions of the same path coexist under api.md:24 and :30; the document never says whether a later version is a new row or an update to the existing one.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "Custom Routes", key the table on the normalized pattern plus the registering schema node — `unique routeAt { normalized_template, schema_node }`, where normalization erases capture names — and rewrite line 82 as: "the key prevents two registrations of the same normalized pattern at one schema node; duplicate-pattern detection across a live trie is the trie insert check (OQ-029)." State explicitly whether registering a changed handler for the same path at a later version is a new row or a new version of the existing one.
- **Verifier note:** The candidate's stronger claim — that two live versions are outright a uniqueness violation — is not established: an update to the same row would give a version chain readable at a historical node. Narrowed to the capture-name normalization defect, which is solid, plus the unresolved versioning question.

### [major] The prepared-node protocol leaves the vote-to-commit window unaddressed for shard-local constraints

- **Where:** docs/api.md:128, docs/distribution.md:407, docs/distribution.md:434, docs/distribution.md:442
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/distribution.md#cross-shard-transactions
- **Evidence:** api.md:128-132 — "**Cross-shard transactions take no lock**: each participant validates against a graph point it pins and appends a prepared node, and the coordinating primary … appends a single commit node that makes every participant's work visible at once." distribution.md:407-415 gives steps 1-4 with "A keeps accepting unrelated writes"; :422 — "A prepared node is not a lock: it excludes nothing"; :434-440 "Why Re-validation Rarely Fails" bounds the risk window to "between the pin and the handoff"; :442-453 restricts only constraints whose *revalidation set crosses shards* to `enforce forward`/`monitor`/`repair into`.
- **Why it is wrong:** The classical reason a 2PC participant holds locks from its yes-vote until the commit is the [vote, commit] window, and the design removes the lock without replacing it or naming the window. B validates against pin P_B and votes yes at t1; because a prepared node excludes nothing, an ordinary local write at B to the same connected component commits at t2; A appends COMMIT at t3. A constraint whose revalidation set is entirely within B is `enforce always`-eligible and is now violated, and the §442 carve-out does not reach it because nothing crossed a shard. "Why Re-validation Rarely Fails" covers only [pin, handoff]. Visibility atomicity still holds; constraint preservation does not.
- **Fix:** Name the choice in docs/distribution.md#cross-shard-transactions and have api.md link to it rather than restate the guarantee. Options: (a) B re-validates on receipt of the COMMIT node and may refuse, which requires a compensating abort path; (b) B's prepared node excludes conflicting writes to the operation's revalidation set until resolved — a lock in all but name, which reinstates the deadlock argument; or (c) B pins a version vector over the touched rows and A's commit node is rejected if any component moved. Add the chosen rule as a subsection between "Why Re-validation Rarely Fails" and the `enforce always` restriction.
- **Verifier note:** Confirmed that neither distribution.md nor OQ-027 addresses the [vote, commit] window; the `enforce always` restriction at :442 covers only cross-shard revalidation sets, not B-local ones. Whether the gap is a real defect or an intended consequence is a design call for the author.

### [major] List/collection types (`[HttpMethod]`) appear in a system table with no production and no entry in types.md

- **Where:** docs/api.md:43, docs/schema/railroad.md:93, docs/schema/types.md:10
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/types.md for the type; docs/schema/railroad.md for the syntax
- **Evidence:** api.md:43 `  methods     : [HttpMethod],     -- which HTTP methods to expose (default: all)`. railroad.md:93-96: `TypeExpr ::= Variant ( '|' Variant )*` / `Variant ::= QName TypeArg* | '(' TypeExpr ( ',' TypeExpr )+ ')'` / `TypeArg ::= QName | Literal`. types.md:10-24 lists the primitives; there is no list, set, or array type.
- **Why it is wrong:** `[HttpMethod]` has no derivation — the only bracketed form is the tuple `'(' TypeExpr (',' TypeExpr)+ ')'`. This is a genuine expressiveness gap rather than a typo: a multi-valued field is otherwise modelled as a `Component` sub-table (tables.md:414), and api.md silently assumes a collection type the language does not have. queries.md:271-273 introduces a second undeclared type constructor for the same reason — `rows.bytes_sent` has type `Table Amount`, with `count :: Table a -> Int` — and `Table` also appears in no production and in no types.md row.
- **Fix:** Either declare the collection types normatively in types.md (`Table a` at minimum, since aggregate signatures depend on it) and add the syntax to railroad.md's `TypeExpr`, or restate api.md:43 as a `Component` sub-table of allowed methods, which is the mechanism tables.md already establishes for repeated values.

### [major] System table declarations use types that no document defines, including a list type with no production

- **Where:** docs/api.md:41-46, docs/api.md:53-56, docs/events.md:383-395, docs/schema/types.md:10-24
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/types.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:43 — `methods     : [HttpMethod],     -- which HTTP methods to expose (default: all)`; api.md:42 and :45 — `table_ref : TableRef unique` and `format_ref : FormatRef`; events.md:385-386 — `queue_type : TypeRef` and `effect_sig : TypeRef`; api.md:191 — `server_id : ServerId`. types.md:10-24 lists the primitive types and includes none of these, and railroad.md's `TypeExpr ::= Variant ( '|' Variant )*` with `Variant ::= QName TypeArg* | '(' TypeExpr ( ',' TypeExpr )+ ')'` has no bracket form.
- **Why it is wrong:** `[HttpMethod]` is a list type the grammar cannot parse and the type system never introduces — and a multi-valued column contradicts tables.md:390 ("There is no embedded product-in-row"), for which the answer elsewhere is a `Component` sub-table. `FunctorRef`, `TypeRef`, `TableRef`, `FormatRef`, `ServerId`, `TokenId` and `Html` appear in normative table declarations with no definition anywhere, so an implementer cannot type-check any system table.
- **Fix:** Add a "System reference types" section to schema/types.md defining `FunctorRef`, `TypeRef`, `TableRef`, `FormatRef` and friends, and replace `methods : [HttpMethod]` with either a `Component` sub-table or a set of `Bool` fields.

### [major] `system.logs.HttpRequest` declares a stored `server_id`, the exact duplication the virtual-column rule removed from `LogSegment`

- **Where:** docs/api.md:190-191, docs/transaction-graph.md:237-241, docs/transaction-graph.md:586-608, docs/open-questions.md:399
- **Normative home:** docs/transaction-graph.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:190-191 — `table system.logs.HttpRequest : LogData {` / `  server_id     : ServerId,`. transaction-graph.md:239-240 — "A segment is written by the server that owns it, so those bytes *are* the answer; a declared field would have been a stored copy of them, free to disagree." OQ-005:399 — "`system.shards.LogSegment` had been hand-rolling this projection as a declared `server` field; that field is **removed**".
- **Why it is wrong:** `origin_server` is a virtual column on every table, typed `:> system.shards.Node`, and the decision record removed exactly this stored copy from another system table on the grounds that it is free to disagree with the identifier. `HttpRequest` keeps it, in an untyped `ServerId` that loses the FK to the node registry, on the highest-volume table in the system.
- **Fix:** Delete `server_id` from the `system.logs.HttpRequest` declaration and note that `origin_server` supplies it, matching transaction-graph.md:230-241.

### [minor] Five types used in api.md's schema declarations are defined nowhere

- **Where:** docs/api.md:42, docs/api.md:43, docs/api.md:44, docs/api.md:191, docs/api.md:198
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md#auto-generated-routes
- **Evidence:** `table_ref : TableRef unique`, `methods : [HttpMethod]`, `format_ref : FormatRef`, `server_id : ServerId`, `client_token : TokenId | NotFound`. A repository-wide grep finds `TableRef`, `FormatRef`, `HttpMethod`, `ServerId`, and `TokenId` only in api.md, and none is declared in types.md or anywhere else.
- **Why it is wrong:** These read as normative declarations in the document that owns HTTP dispatch, and two of them (`TableRef`, `FormatRef`) are the crux of how a route names its target. `TableRef` also does something the design otherwise forbids: naming a schema object from a data row, where the settled pattern is a `:>` to a system table or a compile-checked `Reference` row.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md, replace `table_ref : TableRef unique` with `table_ref :> system.schema.TableNode unique` so the phantom-override check at :113 becomes a foreign key rather than a bespoke validation, and `format_ref : FormatRef` with `format :> system.api.FormatFunctor` — the row it already refers to. Declare `HttpMethod`, `ServerId` (if it survives the `origin_server` fix), and `TokenId` inline in api.md or point at their home in types.md.

### [minor] api.md and cli.md route to and index "views", a schema object the language does not have

- **Where:** docs/api.md:38, docs/api.md:42, docs/api.md:113, docs/cli.md:32, docs/schema/README.md:35, docs/schema/queries.md:5, docs/schema/railroad.md:899
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/queries.md
- **Evidence:** api.md:38 — "driven by a system table — one row per exposed table or view"; :42 — "-- which table or view to expose"; :113-114 — "must reference a table or view that exists in the current schema". cli.md:32 — "| Queries, joins, views, mutation | [schema/queries.md](schema/queries.md) |". Against schema/README.md:35 — "there is no separate schema object called a view"; queries.md:5 the same; railroad.md:899 — "`view` survives only in `refresh view` and `drop materialized view`; there is no `view` declaration."
- **Why it is wrong:** "Table or view" implies two kinds of exposable object where the design has one, and the disjunction leaks into the route rules — `table_ref` and the phantom-override check need no disjunction if a binding is a table. api.md:147's "view refresh" is the legitimate *materialized* view sense; :38 and :113 are not.
- **Fix:** Replace "table or view" with "table or derived table" in docs/api.md lines 38, 42, and 113-114, and change docs/cli.md:32 to "Queries, joins, derived tables, mutation". Keep "materialized view" where it names the storage artifact.

### [minor] The Servant static frame cannot reach any documented URL

- **Where:** docs/api.md:167, docs/api.md:18, docs/api.md:104, docs/tech-stack.md:32
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api.md#http-dispatch
- **Evidence:** api.md:167-171 — "The Servant frame handles the static URL structure (`\"schema\" :> Capture \"ns\" String :> Capture \"name\" String :> Raw`); the `Raw` endpoint delegates to an `IORef (RouteTrie Application)` for runtime-dynamic routing." The documented paths are `/v{N}/records/app.commerce.Order` (:18), `/v{N}/api/orders/{id}/ship` (:19), and `/v{N}/raw/<table-path>` (:104). tech-stack.md:32 carries the same frame, sourced from the OQ-002 spike.
- **Why it is wrong:** The frame is rooted at the literal segment `schema` with exactly two captures, so it matches only `/schema/{ns}/{name}/…`. No request to `/v3/records/…`, `/v3/raw/…`, or an arbitrary custom template ever reaches the `Raw` handler. The OQ-002 frame was for the schema meta-API; api.md reuses it as the data plane, and an implementer wiring it up gets 404s for every documented route.
- **Fix:** In docs/api.md "HTTP Dispatch", show the data-plane frame — a version capture followed by `Raw` over the remaining path, e.g. `Capture "version" Text :> Raw` — and keep `"schema" :> Capture "ns" :> Capture "name" :> Raw` where it belongs, named as the schema meta-API. Note the same distinction at tech-stack.md:25-35.

### [minor] "View" persists as the name for a derived table across five documents after the concept was withdrawn

- **Where:** docs/api.md:38, docs/api.md:42, docs/api.md:114, docs/auth.md:479-481, docs/namespaces.md:5, docs/vision.md:13, docs/cli.md:32, docs/schema/queries.md:3-5
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/queries.md
- **Evidence:** queries.md:4-5 — "All three denote the same kind of thing, so there is no separate schema object called a view". api.md:38 — "one row per exposed table or view"; api.md:42 — "-- which table or view to expose"; auth.md:479-481 — "applications extend it with views rather than by modifying it. A view here is a filter, not a subtype"; namespaces.md:5 — "organizes tables, views, types, and functors"; vision.md:13 — "A query is just a view; a view is just a table."
- **Why it is wrong:** OQ-005:380 records "**There is no view**" as settled and `ViewDecl` as withdrawn; the term survives for the withdrawn concept in five documents, including the system-table comment that tells an implementer what `table_ref` may point at. (Uses meaning *materialized view*, IDE view, or diagram view are fine and are not in scope here.)
- **Fix:** Replace these with "derived table" or "binding", and keep "view" only in "materialized view" and UI senses.

## docs/schema/functors.md

15 findings — 0 blocker, 8 major, 5 minor, 2 nit.

### [major] "On failure, write: reject the transaction" is stated unconditionally in two files, and both withdraw it on the same page

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:111, docs/schema/functors.md:80-86, docs/schema/constraints.md:43, docs/integrity.md:72-77, docs/integrity.md:150-155, docs/schema/railroad.md:436-438
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:111 (varieties table) — "| On failure, write | reject the transaction | reject the transaction |", unqualified. Twenty-five lines earlier, functors.md:84-85 — "| `monitor` | accept | recorded |", "| `repair into <queue>` | accept | recorded and enqueued for remediation |". constraints.md:43 carries the identical row. integrity.md:153 shows an assert addressed by a mode statement: `monitor app.commerce.Order.billingMatch`; railroad.md:436-438 — "An `assert` is addressed by its own name and takes no `/` — including under `repair`".
- **Why it is wrong:** An assert under `monitor` or `repair` accepts the violating write by definition. "Reject the transaction" is the `enforce always`/`enforce forward` behaviour only. Both files state it as an invariant in the table a reader will treat as the specification of what an assert does, and both then withdraw it in an adjacent section.
- **Fix:** Change the "On failure, write" row in both tables to "per the attachment's enforcement mode; default `enforce always` rejects" and link docs/integrity.md#enforcement-modes. If the duplicate-table finding is also applied, only constraints.md:43 needs the edit.

### [major] The foreign-key functor signature `DataId → Either Error Row` is wrong for every `Reference` FK, and integrity.md leans on it

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:15, docs/schema/traits.md:334-335, docs/schema/traits.md:345-347, docs/integrity.md:222-224
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:15 — "| 2 | **Foreign key** | `DataId → Either Error Row` | On commit | …resolves a DataId to a live row in the referenced table |". traits.md:334-335 — "**A field referencing a `Reference` table stores a 2-byte variant tag**, not a 12-byte `DataId`." traits.md:347 — "the FK functor simply resolves a tag instead of a `DataId`." integrity.md:222-224 — "**An existential `:> Any`.** Requires a new concept in the type system, because the FK functor signature `DataId → Either Error Row` cannot resolve without knowing the target table."
- **Why it is wrong:** The normative signature table states a domain the design explicitly says does not hold for one of the two FK cases. Two different domains (a `DataId` and a 2-byte tag) resolved against two different indices are presented as one arrow, and integrity.md uses the incomplete signature as the load-bearing argument for rejecting `:> Any`, so a reader chasing that reasoning meets a form already known to be partial.
- **Fix:** In docs/schema/functors.md's four-kind table change the kind-2 signature to `Ref t → Either Error Row`, add one sentence below the table — "`Ref t` is a `DataId` for a data table and a 2-byte variant tag for a `Reference` table" — and link traits.md#reference-tables-are-code. Update integrity.md:223 to cite the generalised form.

### [major] The event-functor signature `a → EventRef` cannot express the false-to-true transition rule it is paired with; the spike's implementation returns `Maybe`

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:17, docs/schema/functors.md:65-67, docs/schema/functors.md:162, docs/events.md:177-180, spikes/functor-dsl/output.txt:96-103
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:17 — kind 4's signature is `a → EventRef`, "When it runs: On commit, or on a tick". functors.md:162 — "**The condition fires on a `False` → `True` transition, never on merely being true.**" The spike's recorded run at output.txt:96-98 prints `=> Nothing` for tick 1 and tick 3 (no transition) and `=> Just (EventRef {...})` for tick 2, and again at 102-103.
- **Why it is wrong:** `a → EventRef` is total and unary: it always yields an event and sees one value. Firing on a transition needs the pre-state and the post-state and a "do not fire" result. The validated implementation is at minimum `(a, a) → Maybe EventRef` for the stored-field case and threads a `system.events.TriggerState` row for the sampled case. The normative table in functors.md is weaker than the spike it cites as confirmation at functors.md:9.
- **Fix:** In docs/schema/functors.md's four-kind table change the kind-4 signature to `(a, a) → Maybe EventRef`, and add one line below: "the `Maybe` encodes 'no transition, no event'; the sampled `every` form threads a `system.events.TriggerState` row in place of the pre-image."

### [major] "Access rules can be checked statically for consistency and completeness" is claimed in four places, is not what the spike computes, and no OQ tracks it

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:143-145, docs/schema/functors.md:196-198, docs/category-model.md:53, docs/auth.md:419-420, docs/schema/constraints.md:89-90, spikes/functor-dsl/output.txt:152-215
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:144-145 — "access rules can be checked statically for consistency and completeness the same way data constraints can". category-model.md:53 — "access rules can be statically analyzed for consistency (no contradictions, no gaps) before deployment". auth.md:419-420 — "analyzed statically for consistency (no contradictions, complete coverage)". constraints.md:89 — "This also keeps the static completeness analysis tractable". The spike's section 8 (output.txt:152-215) computes assert variety, the exact `bypass access` set, the mixed-conjunct warning, anchoring, the revalidation set, filter placement, the solver classifier, and a cost inventory — never consistency or completeness. No OQ in open-questions.md covers the analysis.
- **Why it is wrong:** An assert body may contain an arbitrary `Read` function application (integrity.md:211 already ships one: ``authed_user `canRead` subject_table``), a `=~` against a `Configuration` pattern resolved at runtime (railroad.md:533), and joins of unbounded length. Containment for the positive conjunctive fragment is decidable (Chandra–Merlin, NP-complete); adding `not` — the Absence shape — pushes containment of UCQs with negation to Π₂ᵖ; adding an uninterpreted user predicate makes it undecidable. "No gaps" is not even well-formed without a specification to compare the policy against, and none exists. This is the payoff the categorical framing is sold on and an implementer has nothing to build.
- **Fix:** Replace the claim at docs/schema/functors.md:143-145 with what the spike supports: "the same structural walk classifies both varieties, computes the exact `bypass access` exemption set, checks anchoring, derives the revalidation set, and checks filter placement." Add one sentence on what is *not* attempted: "Containment and overlap between two access rules is decidable for the positive conjunctive fragment and is not attempted for a body containing `not`, `=~`, or a user-defined predicate." Reduce category-model.md:53 and auth.md:419-420 to links, drop "completeness" or define what it is complete with respect to, and delete the duplicate at functors.md:196-198.
- **Verifier note:** Merged two duplicate candidates. Confirmed against the spike's recorded run, which is the strongest evidence and neither candidate cited it in full.

### [major] The order of operations omits defaults entirely, "address order" is defined nowhere, and step 3 decides per field from a mode that is declared per predicate

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:46-68, docs/schema/functors.md:52-54, docs/schema/railroad.md:178-185, docs/schema/railroad.md:431, docs/schema/functions.md:39, docs/schema/README.md:286-293
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:51 starts the ordering at "**Coerce** the supplied value"; defaults appear in none of the eight steps. functors.md:52 — "run the field's `where` predicates, **in address order**"; a grep confirms "address order" occurs exactly once in all of `docs/`. functors.md:53-54 — "on failure, **the attachment's** enforcement mode decides", against railroad.md:431 — `ValidationRef ::= QName ( '/' Ident )?`, which attaches a mode per predicate. railroad.md:178-181 makes `SeqAlloc` admissible only in a `DefaultClause`; railroad.md:182-185 makes a `SubTableBody` in a `DefaultClause` **construct** a `Component` row "in the same transaction"; functions.md:39 types field defaults as `Tx`. README.md:286-293 shows a merged field carrying three live addresses.
- **Why it is wrong:** Three gaps an implementer hits immediately. (a) Defaults are `Tx`, can allocate a cluster-visible sequence, can construct a whole child row, and can read `authed_user` — yet the ordering never says whether they run before step 1 (and are then coerced and validated) or after step 5, nor whether a constructed component row runs its own steps 1-8 and where those nest. (b) "Address order" is used once and defined nowhere; lexicographic on the path, declaration order, trait-linearization order, and inheritance depth all give different results, and the order decides which failure is reported — which matters most on a `Secret` field, where types.md:374 says only the failing predicate's address is reported. (c) One field can carry `enforce always` on one predicate and `monitor` on another, and nothing says what happens when two predicates with different modes both fail.
- **Fix:** In docs/schema/functors.md#order-of-operations-for-a-field-write: insert a step 0 — "Apply defaults for unsupplied fields, in declaration order; a `SeqAlloc` allocates, and a `Component` sub-table body recursively runs steps 1-7 for the constructed row"; change step 3 to "the strictest mode among the failing predicates decides"; and replace "in address order" with a link to a new definition in docs/schema/README.md#addressing-validations reading "inherited predicates first, in trait-list order as written, then the table's own, in declaration order."
- **Verifier note:** Merged the "address order" candidate into the order-of-operations candidate; they are the same section and the same fix.

### [major] Access asserts run on read, but nothing pins where in query evaluation, nor how a `Redacted` row behaves under `where`, aggregates, and `limit`

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:46, docs/schema/constraints.md:234-243, docs/schema/queries.md:251-276, docs/schema/queries.md:273, docs/schema/railroad.md:624
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:46 titles the ordering "for a **Field Write**" and its eight steps cover only writes. constraints.md:234-236 — "A failed access assertion on a **read** does not abort the query. An assert is row-scoped, so what fails is the row, and **every one of its fields resolves to `Redacted`** — including the key." queries.md:273 — `count :: Table a -> Int`, `sum :: Table Number -> Number`. railroad.md:624 — `LimitClause ::= 'limit' NumLit`. A grep for `Redacted` across `docs/` finds no passage relating it to filters, aggregates, or `limit`.
- **Why it is wrong:** Four concrete, security-relevant consequences are unstated. (a) If `where` runs before redaction, a requester can binary-search a value they may not read (`… where salary > 90000` returning a redacted row or not leaks the predicate's truth); if after, every access-controlled query becomes a scan. (b) `count rows` over a table containing redacted rows either counts them, leaking cardinality, or does not, contradicting constraints.md:237's "the row's presence in the result is what tells a client 'you may not see this'". (c) `sum rows.total` over a column resolving to `Redacted` is ill-typed against `sum : Table Number -> Number`, since `Redacted` is `Null`-derived. (d) `limit 10` where eight rows redact returns ten rows of which eight are opaque, or ten readable rows — different, and unstated.
- **Fix:** Add an "Order of operations for a read" section to docs/schema/functors.md pinning access-assert evaluation relative to filter, join, `group`, `order by`, and `limit` — recommended: redaction is applied at row materialisation, before any predicate naming a field of that row. Add one rule to docs/schema/queries.md#aggregate-functions: an aggregate other than `count` over a table containing redacted rows is a compile-time error, and `count` over such a table is documented as cardinality-revealing.

### [major] The `every` trigger's state is called "a stored last-tick bit" but is realised as an append-only `LogData` row that must be updated, with no `retain` chain

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:173, docs/events.md:179-189, docs/events.md:266-267, docs/schema/traits.md:107-109, docs/schema/traits.md:316-317, docs/schema/railroad.md:270-271
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:173 — "Sampling costs a **stored last-tick bit** per `(trigger, row)`"; events.md:179-180 says the same. events.md:183-188 realises it as `table system.events.TriggerState : LogData { trigger : FunctorRef, subject : DataId, held : Bool, sampled_at : Timestamp }`. events.md:266 and traits.md:316 both say "The `QueueState` field is the **one exemption from append-only in the whole system**". traits.md:107-109 — "A `LogData` table is discarded only by a `retain` chain, and one with no `retain` statement is never discarded at all — silence means keep." railroad.md:270-271 already says "a `system.events.TriggerState` **row** per `(trigger, row)`". A grep finds no `retain system.events.TriggerState` anywhere in `docs/`.
- **Why it is wrong:** Three ways the framing and the realisation disagree. (a) "A bit" versus a four-column row — railroad.md:270 already says row, and the cost argument for preferring a solved crossing is stated against the bit. (b) `held` must be *updated* each tick to mean "held last tick", but the table carries `LogData`, which is append-only everywhere except a `Queue`'s `QueueState` field, and `TriggerState` is not a `Queue` — so the design needs a second exemption, contradicting "the one exemption in the whole system" in two files. (c) If it appends instead, with no `retain` chain declared, "silence means keep" makes `every 30 second` over N rows retain 2N rows a minute forever.
- **Fix:** Decide and record in docs/events.md#every--sampling-for-a-transition: either declare `TriggerState`'s `held` a second narrow append-only exemption — and amend the "one exemption" sentence in events.md:266, traits.md:316, and railroad.md:287-288 together — or keep it append-only and ship a `retain system.events.TriggerState` chain in the same section. In both events.md:179 and functors.md:173 change "bit" to "row", matching railroad.md:270.

### [major] functors.md says all four functor kinds are "defined as rows in system tables"; no such table is declared anywhere, and events.md's `Reference`-table rule forbids one

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:7-8, docs/schema/functions.md:250, docs/events.md:511-519, docs/integrity.md:250, docs/schema/traits.md:353
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:7-8 — "All four are first-class schema objects — defined as rows in system tables, referenced by `FunctorRef`, and encoded in the effect-indexed GADT DSL". A grep for `FunctorRef` across `docs/` finds it as a *column* in `system.api.FormatFunctor` (api.md:55), `system.api.CustomRoute` (api.md:71-75), `system.integrity.Violation` (integrity.md:205), and `system.events.TriggerState` (events.md:184) — never a table *of* functors. events.md:516 and traits.md:353 — "**A `Reference` table is needed exactly where a fact originates outside the schema graph**", with events.md:511-513 removing `system.events.Queue` on exactly that rule. integrity.md:250 — "Functors are schema objects in the `system` shard", which is a different claim.
- **Why it is wrong:** Validation functors are `where` predicates, FK functors are `:>` declarations, path constraints are `assert` bodies, and event functors are `on`/`every` declarations. All four are schema-graph nodes, and mirroring a declaration into a system table is the anti-pattern events.md:511-519 names when it deletes `system.events.Queue`. No document declares such a table; functions.md:250 repeats the same unsupported claim.
- **Fix:** Rewrite docs/schema/functors.md:7-8 as "All four are first-class schema objects — nodes in the schema transaction graph, addressable by `FunctorRef`, and encoded in the effect-indexed GADT DSL", and link events.md#system-tables for the `Reference`-table rule. Change functions.md:250's table row from "Path constraint functors in a system table" to "Path constraint functors addressed by `FunctorRef`".

### [minor] "every path in the schema graph is single-valued by construction" is the stated reason presence is needed, but presence works by traversing `:>` backwards

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:138-140, docs/category-model.md:40, docs/open-questions.md:361, docs/schema/constraints.md:178-179, docs/schema/queries.md:134-138
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:138-140 — "a query in assert position asserts its result is non-empty … Those cover presence and absence, which the equality-only shape could not express at all — every path in the schema graph is single-valued by construction, so there was nothing to quantify over." category-model.md:40 and OQ-005:361 carry the same sentence. constraints.md:178-179 — "every subsequent source must be reached by a join along a declared `:>` edge **in either direction**". queries.md:136 — "Going backwards — from `Account` to the `Suspension` rows that reference it".
- **Why it is wrong:** Composites of declared `:>` morphisms are single-valued; reverse traversal is not, and reverse traversal is exactly what presence and absence quantify over — `self >< Project >< Member` goes backwards along `Member :> Project`. As written the sentence says the graph offers nothing to quantify over and then introduces two shapes that quantify.
- **Fix:** Amend the sentence in all three places to "every *forward* path in the schema graph is single-valued by construction, so an equality had nothing to quantify over; presence and absence quantify over the reverse direction of a `:>` edge, which is a relation rather than a function." Keep the normative copy in category-model.md#path-equivalence-david-spivak-model and reduce functors.md:138-140 to a link.

### [minor] "The commit always succeeds" overstates what an event functor guarantees, and does not describe the `every` or behavior-solved forms

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:20-21, docs/schema/functors.md:17, docs/schema/constraints.md:296-297, docs/category-model.md:59, docs/events.md:143
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Evidence:** functors.md:20-21 — "Kind 4 is asynchronous and decoupled: the commit always succeeds (inserting the queue row is the commit), and the side effect runs later under the event scheduler." functors.md:17 gives kind 4's timing as "On commit, or on a tick". constraints.md:296-297 repeats "inserting the queue row *is* the commit". category-model.md:59 states the accurate version: "The only functor kind that cannot abort a commit". events.md:143 — `every poll_interval emit app.ingest.PriceRefresh { source = self } where active`.
- **Why it is wrong:** Two overstatements. The commit does not "always succeed" — a validation, a `unique` check, or a data assert can still reject it; what holds is that the event functor cannot cause the rejection. And for the `every` form and a behavior-solved crossing there is no triggering commit at all: the scheduler wakes between ticks and writes the queue row in its own transaction, so "inserting the queue row *is* the commit" describes only the `on`-over-stored-fields case, which functors.md:17 itself says is one of two timings.
- **Fix:** Rewrite docs/schema/functors.md:20-21 as "Kind 4 cannot abort a commit. For `on` over stored fields the queue row is written as part of the transaction that triggered it; for `every` and for a solved crossing the scheduler writes it in its own transaction. The side effect runs later." Change constraints.md:296-297 to "and can never abort anything" without the parenthetical.

### [minor] `max_attempts` and `backoff_base` are called "rows in `system.events.QueuePolicy`"; they are columns of it

}
```
railroad.md:261-262 gets it right: "it is a `system.events.QueuePolicy` row, not part of the registration".

### [nit] The `emit` examples elide the payload with a literal `...`, which is not a `RecordField`

### [nit] Four passages use the banned words "just" and "simply"

- **Where:** docs/schema/functors.md:187, docs/schema/tables.md:223, docs/schema/traits.md:347, docs/schema/types.md:141
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

## docs/api-and-rendering.md

14 findings — 0 blocker, 11 major, 3 minor, 0 nit.

### [major] api-and-rendering.md maps absence to `NOT_FOUND` / `Maybe` and collapses the whole `Null` family to JSON null

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:22, docs/category-model.md:156, docs/category-model.md:177, docs/schema/types.md:314-326, docs/vision.md:11
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:22: "Field types are mapped to JSON types; `NOT_FOUND` / `Maybe` fields become nullable JSON (the only place JSON null appears)". category-model.md:156: "Absence is modelled as an ADT family rooted at `Null` — **not** as `Maybe`"; :177: "`Maybe` does appear, but only at the Haskell function boundary". types.md:318 spells the type `NotFound`; types.md:324 has `JsonNull` for an explicit inbound `null`.
- **Why it is wrong:** Three defects in one line. `NOT_FOUND` is a spelling that exists nowhere else and violates the `UpperCamelCase` variant convention (schema/README.md:98). "`Maybe` fields" contradicts the no-`Maybe` rule that vision.md:11 and category-model.md:156 make a headline differentiator. Collapsing the family to one JSON `null` erases the reason-for-absence the model exists to preserve — a client cannot distinguish `Redacted` from `NotGiven`, which is precisely the distinction functors.md:150-152 says the client gets. The parenthetical is also wrong: `JsonNull` exists.
- **Fix:** Rewrite api-and-rendering.md:22 as: "- Field types map to JSON types. A field whose type is an alternation with `Null`-derived variants serialises the variant name, so `Redacted`, `NotGiven` and `NotFound` stay distinguishable; JSON `null` is emitted only for `JsonNull`." State the JSON encoding of `Null` variants normatively in this file's JSON API section and link to it from schema/types.md#absence-types rather than restating it there.

### [major] JSON mapping collapses the `Null`-rooted absence family to bare JSON null and names `Maybe` and `NOT_FOUND`

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:22, docs/schema/types.md:311, docs/schema/types.md:318, docs/schema/types.md:324, docs/category-model.md:162
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/types.md (Absence Types)
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:22 — "Field types are mapped to JSON types; `NOT_FOUND` / `Maybe` fields become nullable JSON (the only place JSON null appears)". types.md:311 — "There is no `NULL`. Absent values are expressed as typed ADTs that extend the `Null` base type. This encodes the *reason* for absence, not just the fact of it." types.md:318 spells it `NotFound`; types.md:324 makes `JsonNull` a first-class variant. category-model.md:162 — "The distinction from `Maybe` is the point. `Nothing` … conflates every reason a value might be missing — which is the same defect NULL has."
- **Why it is wrong:** Four defects in one line. `NOT_FOUND` violates the variant convention (`NotFound`). `Maybe` is not a DataCode type and is the construct category-model.md explicitly rejects. Mapping every `Null`-derived variant to bare null discards the reason for absence — `NotFound`, `Redacted`, `Sealed`, `Erased`, `NotRetained`, `NotGiven` all arrive identical. And "the only place JSON null appears" is false: `JsonNull` carries an inbound document null.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md "JSON API (Third-Party Integration)", replace line 22 with: each `Null`-derived variant serializes as a tagged object, e.g. `{"$absent":"Redacted"}`; JSON `null` never appears in a DataCode response; JSON `null` on input decodes to `JsonNull` inside a `Doc`. Link types.md#absence-types as the home for the variant list rather than restating it.

### [major] Rendering docs describe field-level access hiding; redaction is row-scoped and value-preserving

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:21, docs/api-and-rendering.md:102, docs/schema/constraints.md:234, docs/schema/functors.md:112
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/constraints.md (Redaction Scope)
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:21 — "Access control functors are applied — the JSON response only contains what the token can see"; :102 — "c. Apply access control functors: hide fields/relationships the token cannot see". constraints.md:234-238 — "An assert is row-scoped, so what fails is the row, and **every one of its fields resolves to `Redacted`** — including the key … the row's presence in the result is what tells a client 'you may not see this' as distinct from 'there is nothing here'." constraints.md:240-243 records that exempting/omitting was considered and rejected because surviving or missing fields enumerate row identities under a scan. functors.md:112 — "On failure, read | … | row resolves to `Redacted`".
- **Why it is wrong:** Both statements describe per-field omission, which is precisely the behaviour constraints.md considered and rejected. The settled semantics are per-row and shape-preserving: the row stays in the result with every field, including the key, resolving to `Redacted`.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md rewrite line 21 to "A row failing an access assert is returned with every field, including the key, as the `Redacted` absence variant; nothing is omitted" and line 102 to "c. Apply access control functors: substitute `Redacted` for every field of a row that fails one". Link [schema/constraints.md](schema/constraints.md#redaction-scope) rather than restating. State the one omission case if it exists — a table the client token cannot reach at all under auth.md's schema-level scope.

### [major] api-and-rendering.md calls the binary wire format TBD; OQ-003 settled it as Cap'n Proto with spike evidence

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:9, docs/api-and-rendering.md:14, docs/api-and-rendering.md:115, docs/open-questions.md:103, docs/tech-stack.md:71, docs/storage.md:181
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/storage.md (Wire Format for Replication)
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:9 — "| `application/x-datacode` (TBD) | Servers, thick clients | Binary (TBD) |"; :14 — "The binary format for server-to-server and thick client communication is TBD. Candidates: Cap'n Proto, MessagePack, or a custom format." Against open-questions.md:103-110 "OQ-003: Binary Replication Format ✓ ANSWERED / Cap'n Proto for production; cereal during initial development", tech-stack.md:71-73 "### Binary replication — Cap'n Proto / **Decided (OQ-003).**", and storage.md:179-183 "Wire framing (length-prefix + single-segment message header) is identical."
- **Why it is wrong:** A settled, spike-backed decision is presented as open in the one document a client-integration author reads. MessagePack is specifically excluded by the argument that ruled out Protobuf ("Protobuf requires full parsing; Cap'n Proto mmaps the bytes directly") — MessagePack requires parsing too. api-and-rendering.md:115 then has thick clients consuming "the binary replication protocol", the format it declared TBD.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md "Content-Type Dispatch": set the Format cell to "Cap'n Proto frames (cereal during development)" and replace line 14 with one sentence citing [storage.md](storage.md#wire-format-for-replication) and OQ-003, keeping only requirements this layer adds. Note that the `x-` prefix is deprecated by RFC 6648 and prefer `application/vnd.datacode+capnp`.

### [major] PageRank is defined as in-degree and total degree, computed over "the schema category", oriented to rank sinks, with determinism unstated

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:31, docs/api-and-rendering.md:33, docs/api-and-rendering.md:35, docs/namespaces.md:111, docs/open-questions.md:792
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md#schema-linearization
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:31-35 — "a numeric weight computed per data element using a PageRank-style algorithm over the schema graph: - **Centrality**: how many other tables reference this table (in-degree) - **Integration**: how many relationships this table participates in (total degree) - PageRank is computed on the schema category (tables as nodes, foreign key functors as edges)". namespaces.md:111 — "| `featured` | High-importance, shown prominently | Yes (weighted higher in PageRank) |". OQ-010 (open-questions.md:792-795) — "the computation must be **deterministic**, because two servers computing it independently must reach the same layout. Convergence criteria expressed as 'close enough' are therefore unacceptable without a fixed iteration count and a canonical tie-break."
- **Why it is wrong:** Four problems. In-degree and total degree are not PageRank — PageRank is the stationary distribution of a damped random walk, whose whole point is that a referrer's own rank counts; presenting the degrees as its two components describes a different and much weaker metric. "Computed on the schema category" is ill-posed: a category has all composites, so the intended object is the generating graph of declared `:>` edges. FK edges point dependent → referent, so PageRank over that orientation concentrates mass on lookup sinks (Country, Currency, Status) — the least interesting tables for a UI — and dangling sinks break convergence without an explicit rule. Finally, `featured` is said to raise a table's rank but is not an input in this definition, and OQ-010's determinism requirement (which the storage-clustering consumer makes non-negotiable) is never mentioned here.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md "Schema Linearization", state the algorithm precisely: PageRank over the directed graph of declared `:>` edges with edges **reversed** (referent → dependent), damping `d`, uniform dangling-node redistribution, a fixed iteration count, and a canonical tie-break by fully-qualified name. Demote in-degree and total degree to diagnostics, not inputs. State whether `featured` enters as a personalization vector, a post-rank multiplier, or not at all, and have namespaces.md:111 link here instead of asserting. Cross-link OQ-010's determinism requirement.

### [major] Information-density windowing is inverted, compares a score against an integer, and disagrees with itself on the atomic unit

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:36, docs/api-and-rendering.md:42, docs/api-and-rendering.md:43, docs/api-and-rendering.md:45, docs/ide.md:194
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md#information-density-windowing
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:42-46 — "Each user has a numeric **information density value** (an integer preference). The linearized schema is windowed by this value: - Data elements with importance weight ≤ density value are shown - Data elements above the threshold are hidden or collapsed - Fields on the same table are kept together (the table is the atomic unit for windowing purposes)". Against :31 ("a numeric weight computed … using a PageRank-style algorithm"), :36 ("The result is a ranked list of tables **and fields**"), :38 ("more central data elements appear more prominently"), and ide.md:194 ("a high-density user sees more fields and annotations by default").
- **Why it is wrong:** Two defects. The direction is backwards: with a PageRank weight, higher means more central, so "weight ≤ density value are shown" reveals the least important elements and hides the most — the opposite of the intent at :38. And because a PageRank score is a probability in (0,1), an integer threshold makes the predicate two-valued in practice. Separately, :36 and :43 window fields while :45 makes the table the atomic unit, and ide.md:194 assumes fields — an implementer cannot tell whether fields carry their own weight.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md "Information Density Windowing", define the density value as a cut on the **ranked position** produced at :36, not on the raw weight: assign each table a 1-based rank by descending PageRank score and show tables with `rank ≤ density`. Say once, in that subsection, whether fields are ranked within a shown table or all shown with it, and align ide.md:194 to the answer.

### [major] Per-type render functions have no theme key, no declared table, and no single signature

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:67, docs/api-and-rendering.md:70, docs/api-and-rendering.md:77, docs/api-and-rendering.md:82, docs/schema/functions.md:169, docs/schema/functions.md:176, docs/schema/functions.md:194
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md#themes, with the function-type rule in docs/schema/functions.md#function-types
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:77-80 — "A render function is a **function-valued column on a `Reference` table**"; :70 — "Optional view selection (via HTTP header or user preference) — multiple themes can coexist and be selected per request"; :82-86 — "a theme swap changes every rendered value on every page". The only concrete instance is functions.md:194-195 — `insert system.ui.TypeRender { type_name = "Amount", render = renderMoney }` / `insert system.ui.TypeRender { type_name = "Rate", render = \r -> percent r 2 }`, against functions.md:169 `type Renderer = Amount -> Read Html` and functions.md:176 "**Every function in a field shares one signature**, by construction, because a field has a type." A repository grep finds no declaration of `system.ui.TypeRender` and no theme table anywhere.
- **Why it is wrong:** Two blockers. The `render` column is shown holding an `Amount` renderer in one row and a `Rate` renderer in the next, which no single field type admits under functions.md:176. And `system.ui.TypeRender` is keyed by `type_name` alone with no theme column, so two themes cannot both define a renderer for `Amount` — the premise of the theme-swap claim. Neither api-and-rendering.md nor templates.md names the theme table, its key, the selection header, or the fallback order.
- **Fix:** Declare the tables normatively in docs/api-and-rendering.md "Themes": `table system.ui.Theme : Reference { name : Text unique, stylesheet : Text }` and `table system.ui.TypeRender : Reference { theme :> Theme, type_name :> system.schema.TypeNode, render : Renderer, unique renderFor { theme, type_name } }`, with `type Renderer = Doc -> Read Html` (one signature, dispatch inside) — or state explicitly that render columns are a dependently-typed exception and how the compiler checks it. Name the theme-selection HTTP header and the fallback order (request header → user preference → default theme). Update functions.md:194-195 to match.

### [major] Rendering a `Timestamp` as a relative time requires a clock the effect ladder forbids and a `Moment` nothing supplies

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:69, docs/schema/functions.md:119, docs/schema/functions.md:169, docs/schema/queries.md:401
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/schema/functions.md#function-types
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:69 — "**Render functions per type** — how each DataCode type is rendered to HTML (e.g., `Timestamp` might render as a relative time or an absolute date depending on theme)". Against functions.md:121-134 — "`getCurrentTime` is an `IO` action, and there is no lift from `IO` into any DataCode effect … So a computation that needs the current time takes it as a parameter"; functions.md:169 `type Renderer = Amount -> Read Html`, with no `Moment` parameter; queries.md:401 — "The coordinating server resolves the sample moment once." A grep of templates.md finds no `Moment`.
- **Why it is wrong:** "3 hours ago" is a function of the observation moment. The documented render-function shape is `a -> Read Html`, and a template `Hole` is `Read` and cannot read the clock. No document says how the query's sample moment reaches a render function, so the flagship theming example is the one thing the effect ladder makes unwritable.
- **Fix:** Pick one and say it in docs/schema/functions.md#function-types, referenced from api-and-rendering.md#themes: either widen the renderer to carry the moment — `type Renderer = (Moment, Doc) -> Read Html`, supplied from the query's sample moment (queries.md#every-query-has-a-sample-moment) — or state that relative-time display is a `Behavior`-typed projection on the row rather than a theme concern, and replace the example at api-and-rendering.md:69.

### [major] Thick clients are told to enforce access control and cache materialized views locally, with no scope, revocation, or refresh rule

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:109, docs/api-and-rendering.md:110, docs/api-and-rendering.md:112, docs/api-and-rendering.md:102, docs/open-questions.md:839, docs/storage.md:200
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md#thick-client-local-rendering
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:109-113 — "A thick client holds a local replica of the schema and data (within its access scope). It can: - Render HTML locally using the same algorithm as the server … - Cache materialized views locally for offline or low-latency operation", where step 5c of "the same algorithm" is "Apply access control functors" (:102). Against OQ-012 (open-questions.md:839-841) — "**client pushes carry an invalidation only** — pushing payloads would force the commit path to evaluate every subscriber's access asserts per row, putting an access decision on the write path, which exists nowhere else in the design" — and storage.md:200-206, where a materialized view is pegged to a specific commit node and "Each server maintains its own."
- **Why it is wrong:** If the client runs step 5c, access control is enforced on the client over data the client already holds, so a modified client reads everything in its replica. What "within its access scope" means at replication time — which asserts are evaluated, at what moment, and what happens when a grant is revoked while the client is offline — is stated nowhere, and there is no refresh, invalidation, or staleness rule for a client-held materialized view or for a peg that gets pruned.
- **Fix:** In docs/api-and-rendering.md "Thick Client Local Rendering", state that the server is the sole enforcement point: a client's replica contains only rows the server already released to it; local re-application of asserts is a UI convenience and never a control; and a revocation invalidates the local replica. For local materialized views, either forbid them or specify the pegged commit node, the invalidation signal, and the behaviour when the peg is pruned — linking [storage.md](storage.md#materialization).

### [major] The JSON mapping collapses absence to nullable JSON and calls absent fields `Maybe`, contradicting the no-NULL model

- **Where:** docs/api-and-rendering.md:22, docs/category-model.md:156-177, docs/schema/documents.md:10-13, docs/schema/types.md:314-326
- **Normative home:** docs/api-and-rendering.md
- **Evidence:** api-and-rendering.md:22 — "Field types are mapped to JSON types; `NOT_FOUND` / `Maybe` fields become nullable JSON (the only place JSON null appears)". category-model.md:156 — "Absence is modelled as an ADT family rooted at `Null` — **not** as `Maybe`", and :177 — `Maybe` "appear[s] … only at the Haskell function boundary". documents.md:12-13 — JSON has "exactly one untyped `null` — the construct this project spends most of its design budget eliminating".
- **Why it is wrong:** Three defects in one line: `NOT_FOUND` is not a type name (`NotFound`, per the capitalization rule); `Maybe` is explicitly not how DataCode represents absence; and mapping every `Null`-derived variant onto one JSON null destroys the reason for absence at the API boundary — the exact loss the type family exists to prevent, and asymmetric with the inbound mapping, which preserves `null` as `JsonNull`. There is no normative statement anywhere of how `NotGiven` versus `Redacted` versus `NotFound` serialize.
- **Fix:** Specify the outbound encoding of `Null`-derived variants (e.g. a tagged object `{"absent":"Redacted"}`) in api-and-rendering.md, drop the `Maybe` reference, and fix `NOT_FOUND` to `NotFound`.

### [minor] api-and-rendering.md still calls the binary format TBD after OQ-003 settled it with a spike

OQ-003, open-questions.md:103-104: "### OQ-003: Binary Replication Format ✓ ANSWERED / **Answer**: Cap'n Proto for production; cereal during initial development. See `spikes/capnproto/output.txt`."
- **Why it is wrong:** An answered OQ with a recorded spike is shown as open in the interface document, and the candidate list keeps an option (MessagePack) that fails the same test OQ-003:109 applies to Protobuf — "Protobuf requires full parsing; Cap'n Proto mmaps the bytes directly" — while OQ-003:107 records mmap zero-copy as the deciding property.
- **Fix:** Change api-and-rendering.md:9 to "| `application/x-datacode` | Servers, thick clients | Cap'n Proto |" and replace line 14 with "The binary format is Cap'n Proto (OQ-003, `spikes/capnproto/output.txt`), with `cereal` during development under identical length-prefix framing.
